hints: What do these numbers have in common?
Each can only be divided by 1 and itself.
The primes after 19 are 23 and 29. 21 and 25 aren't prime.
puzzles.explain: These are prime numbers. After 13, the next prime is 17 (15 = 3 × 5).

hints: Try writing each as a power.
Square numbers go 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 (n²). These use a different power.

puzzles.q: 'All A are B' is true. Which statement MUST also be true?
options: Anything that is not B is not A
hints: Draw circle A inside circle B.
If something is outside B, can it be inside A?
'All dogs are mammals' means anything that isn't a mammal isn't a dog. It does NOT mean all mammals are dogs.
puzzles.explain: This is the contrapositive: if it's not B, it can't be A. 'All B are A' doesn't follow.

puzzles.q: If 5 machines make 5 widgets in 5 minutes, how long do 100 machines take to make 100 widgets?
hints: How long does ONE machine take to make ONE widget?
Each machine makes 1 widget in 5 minutes.
If 3 bakers bake 3 cakes in 1 hour, 30 bakers bake 30 cakes in… the same 1 hour.
puzzles.explain: Each machine makes one widget in 5 minutes, so 100 machines make 100 widgets in 5 minutes.

puzzles.q: You flip a fair coin 5 times and get heads every time. What is the chance of heads on the next flip?
hints: Does the coin remember past flips?
Each flip is independent.
A dice that rolled three 6s in a row still has a 1/6 chance of 6 next time.
puzzles.explain: Each flip is independent: still 1/2. Believing otherwise is the 'gambler's fallacy'.

puzzles.q: Thermometer is to temperature as barometer is to…
hints: What does each instrument measure?
'Baro' comes from the Greek for weight or pressure.
Speedometer measures speed. Altimeter measures altitude. Each name hints at what it measures.
puzzles.explain: A thermometer measures temperature. A barometer measures air pressure.

puzzles.q: In a race you overtake the person in 2nd place. What position are you in now?
hints: Whose place do you take when you overtake someone?
You were behind 2nd place, and now you're ahead of them…
If you pass the person in 5th place, you move into 5th place.
puzzles.explain: You take their position: 2nd. The 1st-place runner is still ahead.

puzzles.q: A price rises by 10% and then falls by 10%. Compared with the original, it is now…
hints: Try it with a price of 100.
If 200 rises 50% to 300 and falls 50% to 150, it ends lower, because the fall is on a bigger number.
puzzles.explain: 100 → 110 → 99. The fall is 10% of a bigger number, so it ends 1% lower.

puzzles.q: A cube painted on every face is cut into 27 equal small cubes. How many small cubes have paint on exactly 3 faces?
hints: Which small cubes touch three outer faces?
Think about the corners of the big cube.
A square cut into 9 smaller squares has 4 corner pieces touching 2 edges each. A cube has corners too.
puzzles.explain: Only corner cubes have 3 painted faces, and a cube has 8 corners.

puzzles.q: Exactly ONE of these three people tells the truth. A says: 'B is lying.' B says: 'A and C are both lying.' C says: 'A is telling the truth.' Who tells the truth?
hints: Test each person as the only truth-teller and check for contradictions.
If A were honest, what would that make C's statement?
Worked method: assume X is the only honest one, then check every statement is true for X and false for the others. Throw out cases with 0 or 2+ honest people.
puzzles.explain: If A were honest, C's statement would also be true (two truth-tellers). If C were honest, A would be honest too. If only B is honest: A's claim 'B is lying' is false ✓, C's claim 'A is truthful' is false ✓, and B's claim 'A and C are lying' is true ✓. So B tells the truth.
